newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton turns Air Force One into flying gym.
newsitem.headline: Clinton turns Air Force One into flying gym.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton turned his Air Force One jumbo jet into a flying gym on his way to the Helsinki summit on Thursday, starting his journey with a strenuous workout to help him recover from knee surgery.

Clinton, who tore a tendon in his right knee last Friday and was operated on the same day, was expected to make his way through the summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday and Friday by using a wheelchair and crutches.
In an effort to keep him in shape and to train him to use the crutches, he has been doing physical therapy each day since the operation, which has left his knee immobilised in a brace.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters Clinton began his flight to Helsinki with a workout involving parallel bars and weights. "It's a serious deal," he said. "You, like, sweat."

He said the aircraft had been slightly modified to help Clinton get around, with the doors to his cabin and office removed. Clinton was wheeled onto and off of the plane, and lifted to its door with special elevator-trucks.
Clinton caught his heel on a step at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman early last Friday, tearing the quadriceps tendon connecting the kneecap to the upper thigh in his right leg.
The accident will keep Clinton on crutches for about eight weeks and the president's doctors said it is likely to take him six months before he can return to his regular running and golf.
